problem: Determine the equation of the level curve that passes through the point $P(1,0)$ for the function $f(x,y)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the value of the function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1,0) & =\frac{1}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1+0+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the level curve that passes through $P(1,0)$ is the $\frac{1}{2}$-level curve.

Recall that the level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equation

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

In our case, we're interested in $c=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2 & ={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1 \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the level curve that passes through $P(1,0)$ is the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1.$
